Hi all, is there consensus on what should happen when the execution client receives a payload where the withdrawals break the monotonically increasing index rule ? It seems to me like there should be no verification on the EL-side whatsoever, because that would mean the EL needs to save the last index somewhere, but just wanted to confirm in order to have that in mind while writing the test vectors... <dannyryan> yeah, interesting question mario The spec does say: > a monotonically increasing index, starting from 0, as a uint64 value that increments by 1 per withdrawal to uniquely identify each withdrawal The fact that it is in the EL spec kind of implies that it would be a validity condition (rather than just saying, "there is an index") It was written there to be informative rather than normative. And adding additional verificaiton logic and overhead in EL does not buy us anything other than complexity (as I see it currently) <dannyryan> I would be in favor of turning that bullet point into "a `uint64` index identifying the withdrawal" <dannyryan> cc: <@539495253418180618> i think the EIP is pretty clear about what is and is not a validity condition for the EL im happy to be less precise if this point is confusing in the EIP but the intent was to provide as much information as possible, as clients have more optionality around optimized storage/retrieval of withdrawal data if they know there is extra structure here around the index I did not interpret this as an EL validity condition fwiw so it sounds like we should be storing the last valid withdrawal index and verify each withdrawal in monotonically increasing? This may not happen soon enough for this <@833706406699073536> Why is hard? Capella is deterministic. I'm forking perfectly fine in my interop Why would you do it if we're enforcing it and there's a trust assumption anyway <@199561711278227457> coming back to timing: just set TTD to zero. Bellatrix is on an epoch and capella on another one. There's no room for timing issues Yeah, that was my original thought and the reason I have not implemented this check, but I was trying to confirm if <@539495253418180618>' intention was for ELs to verify If you guys enforce it then I'll move to remove that index from the beacon state 🙂 <dannyryan> I'm saying don't enforce on EL. and if the fact that that statement is under "specification" in the EIP implies otherwise, we should edit it <dannyryan> and we should have an EL test with scrambled withdrawal indices and duplicates and EL should be fine with it Haha hope you're saying under reorgs... Like forcing El clients to not enforce something is murky <ralexstokes> the idea is to write tests that enforce the spec, and the spec says (or implies if it’s not clear rn) that the CL verifies all of the data coming from the engine API to the EL, the EL just blindly applies them to the world state I don't really mean to be getting into a flame over the same kinds of things as before. But I find wrong enforcing behavior that is not strictly necessary. If the EL dev wants to check that the withdrawal amount corresponds to the amount in the beaconstate Balance, and somehow they have access to the right information, the spec should not forbid them from doing this check. The spec can allow them to not do it, but not forbid them to do it unless there's a clear reason to. To me testing that the EL does not check for something under a malformed input is equivalent to the issue we already had on justification bits

excerpts.author: marioevz
excerpts.content:
Hi all, is there consensus on what should happen when the execution client receives a payload where the withdrawals break the monotonically increasing index rule ?

It seems to me like there should be no verification on the EL-side whatsoever, because that would mean the EL needs to save the last index somewhere, but just wanted to confirm in order to have that in mind while writing the test vectors...

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<dannyryan> yeah, interesting question mario

The spec does say:
> a monotonically increasing index, starting from 0, as a uint64 value that increments by 1 per withdrawal to uniquely identify each withdrawal

The fact that it is in the EL spec kind of implies that it would be a validity condition (rather than just saying, "there is an index")

It was written there to be informative rather than normative. And adding additional verificaiton logic and overhead in EL does not buy us anything other than complexity (as I see it currently)

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <dannyryan> I would be in favor of turning that bullet point into "a `uint64` index identifying the withdrawal"

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: i think the EIP is pretty clear about what is and is not a validity condition for the EL

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: im happy to be less precise if this point is confusing in the EIP but the intent was to provide as much information as possible, as clients have more optionality around optimized storage/retrieval of withdrawal data if they know there is extra structure here around the index
